title: Ultra Lowrate Image Compression with Semantic Residual Coding and Compression-aware Diffusion

source_version.publication: Proceedings of the 42nd International Conference on Machine Learning, PMLR volume 267 (2025)
source_version.version_basis: official publisher linked PDF acquired on retrieval date, frozen by SHA-256

summary: Independent-noise posterior is incompatible with the deterministic reverse conditional used for core CDM and downstream training derivation. Released index coding omits required side information; its historical experimental effect is unresolved.

problems.title: Incompatible conditional distributions in the core CDM derivation
problems.claim: The independent-noise conditional can also be represented by the proposed reverse kernel and its deterministic coefficient settings.
assumptions: Independent standard Gaussian per-time noises from stated proof
problems.check: Compare conditional covariance under independent noise with zero covariance in the deterministic kernel; also compare cross-covariances.
problems.result: (1-a_(n-1)) I > 0 versus 0 for the same conditional; cross-covariance 0 versus sqrt((1-a_(n-1))(1-a_n)) I.
problems.counterevidence: A shared-noise dependent coupling preserves the marginals and yields the deterministic update. Theorem B.3 coefficient conditions can be necessary marginal conditions, but do not identify the conditional.
problems.impact: Invalid derivation directly supplies core CDM sampler and ELBO argument. Empirical performance not refuted.

correction.statement: Use a shared standard Gaussian E and constant gamma to define a dependent joint; deterministic transition then follows by elimination.
correction.limits: Drops conditional independence; does not repair full stochastic or training/ELBO derivation.

focused_acceptance.assumptions_and_decisive_evidence: The source states independent per-time Gaussian noises at an internal nondegenerate step, yet the default reverse conditional has eta=sigma_n=0. Conditional covariance is (1-a_(n-1))I>0 under independence and zero under the deterministic kernel; the checked a_(n-1)=16/25, a_n=9/25 example gives 9/25 versus zero. Marginal moment matching cannot identify that conditional.
focused_acceptance.counterevidence_and_limits: A shared-noise coupling preserves the marginals and recovers the deterministic update. It changes the joint distribution and therefore does not validate the independent-noise posterior or the subsequent ELBO argument.
focused_acceptance.core_dependency_and_severity: The invalid conditional is used in the core CDM sampler and training derivation (Theorem 5.2 and Eqs.37-38). Major is retained on this demonstrated core dependency, without requiring a benchmark loss.
focused_acceptance.correction_scope: The shared-noise construction is a verified local analytic repair only; a full stochastic/training-ELBO repair remains unverified.

problems.title: Uncharged decoding information in released text coder
problems.claim: Counted semantic payload represents the encoded token indices.
problems.location: nn_indices.py 22-76; inference_res.py 82-105; inference_res_pfo.py 93-116; paper p.4 Eq.2/p.5/p.13 A.3/p.15 Fig.16
assumptions: Codec accepted CPU integer index inputs [333] and [444]
Charged payload contains arithmetic bytes only
problems.check: Both inputs produce identical numeric coder inputs, but recovery requires different alphabet.
problems.result: The counted payload alone is non-injective; required side information is passed in memory and uncharged.
problems.counterevidence: A complete shared or serialized protocol could fix it; paper states total rate includes text; historical experiment code not established.
problems.impact: Supported release defect; magnitude and effect on published RD comparisons Needs Evidence.

correction.statement: Specify and count complete decoding information or a genuinely shared model/framing protocol.
correction.limits: No missing-bit estimate or corrected BD rate verified.

focused_acceptance.source_location: nn_indices.py 22-76; inference_res.py 82-105; inference_res_pfo.py 93-116; paper p.4 Eq.2/p.5/p.13 A.3/p.15 Fig.16
focused_acceptance.assumptions_and_decisive_evidence: Static inspection of the pinned nn_indices.py and inference_res.py confirms per-input alphabet/CDF construction and charging only arithmetic bytes. CPU index inputs [333] and [444] produce identical numeric coder inputs but need different alphabets for reconstruction, so the charged payload alone is non-injective. No author code was run.
focused_acceptance.counterevidence_and_limits: The paper says total rate includes text, and an explicitly shared or serialized decoding protocol could resolve the defect. The 2026 release is not bound to the 2025 experimental implementation.
focused_acceptance.core_dependency_and_severity: Minor is retained for the established release protocol defect. Historical rate-distortion impact is unresolved because the release-to-experiment dependency is unestablished, not because a measured score loss is required.
focused_acceptance.correction_scope: The report correctly asks for complete, counted decoding information and does not invent missing-bit totals or corrected BD rates.

clarifications.summary: At endpoint coefficient of z0 vanishes; zc branch is an estimator and loss zeroing can be deliberate masking, not exact inversion.
